provenance.instrument: Code of the Township of Spring (Berks County), Chapter 450 Zoning (Zoning Ordinance of 2015, Ord. No. 415, 6-22-2015, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: Chapter 450 adopted 6-22-2015 by Ord. No. 415. eCode360 New Laws (read 2026-11-12) list Ord. 473 to 476 (fire code, code enforcement, traffic). None amends Chapter 450.
provenance.code_current_through_note: Date carried from the towns index. The print view read on 2026-11-12 shows no currency line. New Laws lists items to 2026-08-10, none zoning.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment or in-law provision
'No land or building or structure shall be used or occupied except for a use permitted in the zoning district' (450-302A). LDS and MDS permit only the single-family detached dwelling as housing

SS and U permit by right (with site plan review) two-family detached (duplex) and semidetached (twin) dwellings. 'Single-family to multifamily conversions' are also listed, but must meet the multifamily rules (three or more units, a tract of 3 to 5 acres) (450-310B, 450-311B, 450-324B(44), (97))
Lot area in the district tables is per dwelling unit for residential uses: LDS 10,000, MDS 8,000, SS 5,000, U 3,500 sq ft with public sewer and water (450-308F to 450-311F)
Two principal buildings on a lot with a residence must each meet the rules as if on a separate lot, including lot size, and need land development approval (450-402B)
Accessory buildings: 15 ft high. All of them together at most 50% of the house floor area (600 sq ft allowed in any case, 1,500 on two acres). Not in required yards (450-327C(1))
Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit of 3 bedrooms or less (Table 7.1)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Spring Township Zoning (springtwpberks.org). Residential districts: RHA, RC, RS, LDS, MDS, SS, U. Read on eCode360 in a browser, the chapter print view, searched in the page. Searched for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, apartment accessory, in-law, granny, ECHO, elder cottage, caretaker, guest house, carriage, second dwelling, accessory residential, servant, au pair, accessory unit, tiny, dependent, relative, family member, tenant, conversion, kitchen. No ADU provision. 450-327C(1)(e) does not limit 'other uses not mentioned so long as they are clearly accessory to the principal permitted use'. A second dwelling unit is read as not clearly accessory, since 450-401 and 450-402B treat added dwellings as principal uses. RHA, RC and RS district tables were not read in full. A second house on a lot large enough for two (450-402B, each as if on its own lot, with land development approval) is a further path, not an ADU.

status.note: The code has no ADU text. LDS and MDS list only the single-family detached dwelling.

path.note: A second unit is not a permitted use in LDS or MDS. It needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). No unlisted-use special exception was found.

value.name: Two-family detached (duplex) or semidetached (twin) dwelling
value.conditions: Permitted by right with site plan review. Lot area is per dwelling unit, 5,000 sq ft each, so 10,000 for two units with public sewer and water. 2 parking spaces per unit.

value.name: Two-family detached (duplex) or semidetached (twin) dwelling
value.conditions: Permitted by right with site plan review. Lot area is per dwelling unit, 3,500 sq ft each, so 7,000 for two units. 2 parking spaces per unit.

value.name: Single-family to multifamily conversion
value.conditions: Permitted by right with site plan review. 'Shall comply with all applicable requirements for multifamily dwellings (single-family attached dwellings or garden apartments).' Those standards (450-324B(44)) need a tract of at least 3 acres (townhouses) or 5 acres (garden apartments), 10 to 15 units an acre, open space and public sewer and water. Multifamily means three or more units (450-202). Not a path for an ordinary house.
value.note: Tract minimum read by the reviewer in 450-324B(44). 3 acres is the smaller of the two tract sizes.

alternatives.note: Not ADUs. 'TWO-FAMILY DETACHED DWELLING ... commonly called a duplex.'

historic_bypass.note: No ADU text, so no historic path.

max_height_ft.note: Accessory building rule, not an ADU rule. 'No accessory building to the principal residential use shall have a height greater than 15 feet.'

accessory_floor_area_total_sqft.note: Cumulative accessory floor area may not exceed 50% of the principal building floor area, or 600 sq ft if that is larger. 1,500 sq ft on lots of two acres or more. No fixed number.

setback_side_ft.note: Not in required yards. In the rear yard the setback is the district's one-side yard. 5 ft where the yard abuts an alley.

setback_rear_ft.note: May sit in the required rear yard at the district's one-side yard distance.

max_adus.note: Reading: 0 means the code allows no ADU. 'No more than one principal use shall be permitted on a lot'.

spaces_required.note: No ADU row. 'Dwelling, 3 bedrooms or less: 2 per dwelling unit'.

min_lot_sqft.note: Per dwelling unit for residential uses, with both public sewer and water. Width 80 ft. Impervious 55%. 43,560 sq ft without both public sewer and water. 450-408B lets a lot of record below these figures be built on if yards are met.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Table footnote: '* Per dwelling unit for residential uses.' A house and a second unit would need twice this area.
